memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, with a thick
cloud over the mountain, and a very loud trumpet blast. Everyone in the camp
trembled." - Ex 19:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The third day arrives, and it is overwhelming. Thunder, lightning, thick cloud,
and a trumpet blast so loud that an entire nation trembles.

Notice that trumpet. No human being was blowing it. It sounded from the mountain
itself.

This is God making Himself unmistakable. There would be no possibility of Israel
later claiming they had misunderstood or that Moses had made it up. Hundreds of
thousands of people experienced it at once.

Notice the response: everyone trembled. Not some. Everyone.

There is a kind of fear that Scripture commends, and this is it. Not terror that
drives us away, but awe that recognises what we are dealing with. "The fear of
the LORD is the beginning of wisdom" (Prov 9:10).

Much modern Christianity has lost this almost entirely. We speak of God as a
friend, which He graciously is, and forget that He is the one before whom
mountains smoke. Isaiah saw the Lord and said, "Woe to me! I am ruined!" (Isa
6:5). John, who had leaned on Jesus' chest, fell at His feet as though dead (Rev
1:17).

Both men were then lifted up and sent. But they trembled first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did you last feel genuine awe before God?
2. Has your familiarity with God cost you your reverence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, restore my awe. Let me know You as friend without ever forgetting who You
are. Amen.
